definition: Estimating the per-pixel foreground opacity (alpha matte) for precise cut-outs of hair and translucent boundaries — finer than segmentation.
details: Estimating the per-pixel foreground opacity (alpha matte) for precise cut-outs of hair and translucent boundaries — finer than segmentation.

explainer.lead: Image matting estimates per-pixel foreground opacity, the alpha matte, for precise cut-outs. It captures hair and translucent boundaries more finely than segmentation.

tiers.eli5: Like peeling a sticker off a photo so precisely that even wispy hair edges come away cleanly.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use matting when a binary mask is too coarse, such as fine hair or glass; a common pitfall is that soft, translucent edges are where naive masks fail most.
tiers.paperLevel: Estimating the per-pixel foreground opacity (alpha matte) for precise cut-outs of hair and translucent boundaries; finer than segmentation.

explainer.example: Producing an alpha matte that separates a subject's hair from the background at each pixel.
